findings.title: Off-by-one slice drops the newest invoice on every page
findings.explanation: `rows.slice(1, limit + 1)` starts at index 1, so the first (newest) row is always discarded. Each page also returns only `limit - 1` invoices when more rows exist. Because `next_before` is taken from the last row of the sliced page, the dropped row is never returned on any later page either. Use `rows.slice(0, limit)`. If the page is full and `hasMore` is true, `page[page.length - 1]` is then the `limit`-th row, which is the correct cursor.

findings.title: No test coverage for pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: The slice bug would have been caught by a test. Add tests for: fewer than `limit` rows, exactly `limit` rows (`next_before` should be null), `limit + 1` rows (`next_before` should be the id of the `limit`-th row), and zero rows. Also assert that the returned ids are contiguous across consecutive pages.

findings.title: Clarify the limit + 1 over-fetch
findings.explanation: Add a short comment, or a named variable such as `const fetchCount = limit + 1`, explaining that the extra row only detects whether another page exists and is never returned. This stops a later reader from 'fixing' it.

Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
